note: Lesson 6.1 (discovery and scoping) has no n8n build: its solved problem is a written, signed scope, not a workflow.

walk.title: Solve it: from call notes to a signed scope
walk.sample: Okonkwo Pharmacy, Bodija · 30-minute call notes · seven ideas on the wish list

steps.say: Mrs Okonkwo gave us seven ideas in five minutes. Before any bot, we turn her call into one project she can sign: mapped, priced and bounded.
show: Discovery notes: last Monday, hour by hour

steps.say: Score each idea from one to five on pain, feasibility and risk. Pain is time and money lost; feasibility is whether the data and rules exist.
The AI doctor is declined outright: medical advice stays with the pharmacist. Refill reminders and low-stock alerts score highest, and the WhatsApp bot can be phase 2.
show: Refill reminders + low-stock alerts → do now

steps.say: Now confirm the numbers, using her own figures, not ours. About 12 hours a week across two staff, and about six stock-outs or expiries a month.
show: ~12 h/week on calls and stock checks

steps.say: Be conservative and count only the share the automation really takes over. That gives about 238,000 naira a month, and a 450,000 naira build pays back in a little over two months.
The scope's goal is measurable: no missed refills or stock-outs on the top 40 items, and staff time under two hours a week.
show: Goal: no missed refills or stock-outs (top 40)

steps.say: In scope, one line each. Reminders use an approved WhatsApp utility template, only to customers who consented, and never name the medicine, because health information is sensitive.
show: "Your refill … is due on {{date}}. Reply YES…"

steps.say: The section beginners skip is out of scope. Medical advice, a chatbot, supplier ordering, the staff rota, marketing and any app are all listed, so nothing creeps in for free.
show: supplier ordering · staff rota · marketing · any app

steps.say: List what the client provides, like the verified WhatsApp number, so verification starts in week one. Acceptance tests are specific, so no one can say it doesn't work well enough.
show: Client provides: verified number, consented list
Consent recorded for every customer messaged

steps.say: Price and changes are written down too: half to start, half at go-live, a monthly fee for running it, and new requests quoted separately.
Book 20 minutes. Show the before-and-after map first, then the numbers, then the out-of-scope list, so you're both clear what this isn't.
show: Order: map → numbers → out of scope

steps.say: Ask her to name one more thing she expected. If it's missing, decide together: add it with a price, or put it in phase 2. Only then send the scope to sign, and the first invoice.
show: Missing item → add with price, or phase 2

walk.end: That's the scope: one strong project, the client's own numbers, six things out of scope, and tests you can actually run at handover.
